papers.title: Rethinking Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation: From Alignment Coverage to Supervision Reliability
papers.abstract: Abstract  On-Policy Distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own generations using teacher feedback. With different tokenizers, comparing teacher and student predictions requires alignment at both sequence and vocabulary levels. In this paper, we examine whether expanding this alignment coverage improves learning. Across three heterogeneous teacher--student pairs on mathematical reasoning and code generation, strict 1:1 groups already cover most student-generated tokens despite substantial vocabulary mismatch. On responses sampled from the students before distillation, the shared vocabulary retains nearly all teacher and student probability mass at strictly aligned positions on average. Restricting reverse KL to a student-selected top-16 subset of the shared vocabulary at each strict position achieves accuracy comparable to full shared-vocabulary OPD, outperforming the evaluated cross-tokenizer baselines. Adding mean squared error supervision on span log-probabilities in mismatch groups gives complete supervision coverage, yet reduces accuracy. At checkpoints from training with only the strict loss, the span gradients show weak or negative directional agreement with the strict gradients and grow in magnitude relative to them. These diagnostics may help explain the accuracy drop from adding span supervision. Our findings motivate a shift from maximizing alignment coverage to prioritizing supervision reliability: compact supervision at strict positions can be more effective than broader coverage that introduces weakly aligned or conflicting training signals.

ru.title: Качество обучающего сигнала превосходит полноту покрытия в дистилляции моделей
ru.desc: В работе исследуется On-Policy Distillation (OPD) — метод обучения студент-моделей на их собственных выборках с использованием обратной связи от учителя. Авторы анализируют проблему выравнивания предсказаний учителя и студента при использовании разных токенизаторов на уровне последовательностей и словарей. Они обнаруживают, что строгое 1:1 выравнивание токенов охватывает большинство выборок студента, несмотря на значительное несовпадение словарей, и что ограничение KL-дивергенции топ-16 подмножеством общего словаря достигает сравнимой точности. Результаты показывают, что надёжность сигнала обучения важнее полноты покрытия выравнивания, и компактный контроль на строго выровненных позициях эффективнее, чем расширенное покрытие с конфликтующими градиентами.

en.title: Prioritize Reliable Supervision for Better Learning in OPD
en.desc: This paper introduces On-Policy Distillation (OPD), a method where a student model learns from its own outputs with guidance from a teacher model. It emphasizes the importance of aligning predictions at both the sequence and vocabulary levels when comparing the teacher and student. The study finds that focusing on a strict 1:1 alignment can effectively cover most of the student-generated tokens, even with vocabulary mismatches. Additionally, it suggests that prioritizing reliable supervision over broader alignment can lead to better learning outcomes, as adding more complex supervision may introduce conflicting signals that hinder accuracy.

zh.title: 优先考虑监督可靠性，提升学习效果
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为“在政策蒸馏”（OPD）的方法，该方法通过教师反馈训练学生模型。研究发现，在不同的分词器下，教师和学生的预测需要在序列和词汇层面上进行对齐。通过扩展这种对齐覆盖范围，能够改善学习效果。结果表明，尽管词汇存在显著不匹配，严格的1:1分组已经覆盖了大部分学生生成的标记，因此在监督学习中，优先考虑监督的可靠性比单纯追求对齐覆盖更为有效。

papers.title: DuoMatching: Joint-Marginal Distribution Matching for Few-Step Video Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract  Streaming video generation has benefited from distribution matching distillation (DMD), which matches the joint distribution of video frames to a video teacher's approximation of the real video distribution. Although this joint matching mitigates drift during autoregressive rollouts, limitations remain in visual quality and semantic alignment. To address these limitations, we propose DuoMatching, a distribution matching framework that approximates the real video distribution through a unified joint-marginal formulation. On top of existing joint matching formulations, the additional marginal matching objective provides dedicated frame-level supervision from an image generator, transferring complementary visual and semantic priors from it. To apply this frame-level supervision in video generation, we introduce LatentBridge to resolve the latent representation mismatch between the video student and the image teacher. Latent Variation Sampling further distributes such frame-level supervision across distinct temporal segments, reducing redundancy. Experiments demonstrate that DuoMatching improves visual quality, composition, and semantic alignment while largely preserving motion dynamics. Human evaluations show overall preference rates above 80% against all evaluated baselines. The project page is available at https://johnzhan2023.github.io/DuoMatching/.

ru.title: Двойной подбор распределений для высококачественной генерации видео
ru.desc: В работе предлагается DuoMatching — фреймворк для генерации видео потоком, который использует дистилляцию с подбором распределений. Метод аппроксимирует истинное распределение видео через объединённую формулировку совместного и маргинального подбора распределений, где маргинальное соответствие добавляет супервизию на уровне отдельных кадров от генератора изображений. Для синхронизации латентных представлений между моделью-студентом видео и учителем-изображений введён LatentBridge, а Latent Variation Sampling распределяет супервизию по временным сегментам, снижая избыточность. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что метод значительно улучшает визуальное качество, композицию и семантическое соответствие кадров, при этом сохраняя динамику движения.

en.title: DuoMatching: Elevating Video Generation Quality through Advanced Distribution Matching
en.desc: This paper introduces DuoMatching, a new framework for improving streaming video generation by enhancing the matching of video frame distributions. It combines joint and marginal distribution matching to provide better visual quality and semantic alignment in generated videos. The method includes a LatentBridge to align representations between video and image models, and uses Latent Variation Sampling to effectively distribute supervision across time segments. Experiments show that DuoMatching significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of visual fidelity and coherence, with high preference rates from human evaluators.

zh.title: DuoMatching：提升视频生成质量的新框架
zh.desc: 本论文提出了一种新的视频生成框架，称为DuoMatching，旨在提高视频的视觉质量和语义一致性。DuoMatching通过统一的联合边际公式来近似真实视频分布，并在现有的联合匹配基础上增加了边际匹配目标，以提供帧级监督。该方法引入了LatentBridge，解决了视频学生与图像教师之间的潜在表示不匹配问题。实验结果表明，DuoMatching在视觉质量、构图和语义对齐方面都有显著提升，且运动动态得以大幅保留。

papers.title: From Evidence to Action: How Tool-Using Agents Fail
papers.abstract: Abstract  Tool-using agents make consequential changes to external state, yet correct outcomes do not guarantee that their actions were supported by evidence established beforehand. We study where this evidence-to-action chain breaks as agents move from deciding whether to act to executing single actions and dependent workflows. Across ten model-harness configurations, strong static action assessment can coexist with much weaker interactive execution. Failures often begin before execution: agents stop with incomplete investigation or act before required evidence is established. Once required evidence is obtained, single-action execution is usually reliable, while multi-action workflows additionally expose unresolved prerequisites and incomplete execution. For this analysis, we introduce SafeActBench, comprising 656 cases across six operational domains and five protocols that progress from static action judgment and investigated non-action to single- and multi-action workflows. A provenance-bound Evidence Ledger and deterministic trajectory evaluator track what information was established, when actions occurred, and whether downstream dependencies were satisfied. These results show that failures arise not only from missing information, but also from how agents use established evidence when deciding and executing actions.

ru.title: От доказательства к действию: почему агенты ошибаются в цепочке рассуждений
ru.desc: Исследование показывает, что агенты, использующие инструменты, часто совершают ошибки не из-за недостатка информации, а из-за неправильного использования уже установленных доказательств при принятии решений и выполнении действий. Авторы выявили, что сбои происходят на разных этапах: агенты могут прекратить расследование, не завершив его, или начать действие до установления необходимых доказательств. Для анализа этой проблемы создан SafeActBench — набор данных из 656 тестовых случаев с инструментом Evidence Ledger, который отслеживает, какая информация была установлена и когда произошли действия. Исследование демонстрирует, что даже сильные модели проявляют слабость при выполнении многошаговых рабочих процессов, хотя обычно хорошо справляются с отдельными действиями после получения всех требуемых доказательств.

en.title: Bridging Evidence and Action in Tool-Using Agents
en.desc: This paper investigates how tool-using agents make decisions and execute actions based on evidence. It reveals that while agents may assess actions effectively in a static context, their performance can decline during interactive execution. The study introduces SafeActBench, a framework that evaluates agents across various scenarios, highlighting that failures often stem from incomplete investigations or premature actions. The findings emphasize the importance of both having the right information and effectively utilizing it during decision-making and execution processes.

zh.title: 证据与行动：代理执行中的关键链条
zh.desc: 本文研究了工具使用代理在执行动作时如何依赖于事先建立的证据。我们发现，尽管静态动作评估表现良好，但在交互执行过程中却常常出现较弱的表现。代理在执行之前可能会因为调查不充分或在证据未建立前就开始行动而导致失败。一旦获得所需证据，单一动作的执行通常是可靠的，但多动作工作流则可能暴露出未解决的前提条件和不完整的执行。

papers.title: AutoSciBench: Autonomous Benchmark Generation for Evaluating Scientific Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  As agents rapidly evolve, existing benchmarks can become saturated, limiting their ability to distinguish capabilities and reveal remaining failure modes. Particularly in scientific domains, constructing and updating benchmarks requires substantial time, labor, and domain expertise, making it difficult to keep evaluation aligned with advances in agent capabilities. We address this challenge by investigating whether scientific-agent benchmarks can be automatically generated and iteratively adapted as agent capabilities evolve. We introduce AutoSciBench, a framework that represents each task as a high-level concept specifying the scientific domain, data modality, and required reasoning approach, together with a low-level recipe specifying how the question, environment, and ground-truth answer are constructed and verified. Agents attempt to solve each task, producing solver trajectories and corresponding judge feedback which AutoSciBench uses to revise the recipe or concept, closing observed shortcuts and shifting tasks toward raw-data re-examination, interpretation of intermediate results, and evidence integration. Experience distilled from completed refinement trajectories further guides new concept generation, allowing lessons from earlier task refinement to inform subsequent benchmark construction. Starting from existing benchmarks, we evaluate AutoSciBench across computational biology, materials science, and clinical imaging. Generated benchmarks reduce average solver accuracy by 22.4 and 25.5 percentage points relative to the human-curated benchmarks in computational biology and materials science, respectively, while generated tasks receive higher average quality ratings across all three domains, suggesting that scientific-agent evaluation can adapt as agent capabilities advance.

ru.title: Автоматическая адаптация научных бенчмарков к развитию агентов
ru.desc: Авторы представляют AutoSciBench — фреймворк для автоматического создания и итеративной адаптации научных бенчмарков по мере развития способностей агентов. Каждая задача представляется высокоуровневой концепцией (научная область, модальность данных, требуемый тип рассуждений) и низкоуровневым рецептом для конструирования вопроса, окружения и эталонного ответа. Система анализирует траектории решений агентов и отзывы судей для автоматического уточнения задач, закрывая найденные лазейки и смещая фокус на более глубокий анализ данных. На примерах вычислительной биологии, материаловедения и клинической визуализации показано, что автоматически сгенерированные бенчмарки снижают точность решателей на 22-25 процентных пункта и получают более высокие оценки качества.

en.title: Evolving Benchmarks for Evolving Agents
en.desc: This paper presents AutoSciBench, a framework designed to automatically generate and adapt benchmarks for scientific agents as their capabilities evolve. It defines tasks using high-level concepts and low-level recipes, allowing for dynamic updates based on agent performance. By analyzing solver trajectories and feedback, AutoSciBench iteratively refines tasks to address weaknesses and enhance evaluation quality. The results show that the generated benchmarks are more challenging and receive better quality ratings compared to traditional human-curated benchmarks in various scientific fields.

zh.title: 智能体评估的自适应基准生成
zh.desc: 随着智能体的快速发展，现有的基准测试可能会饱和，限制其区分能力和揭示失败模式的能力。特别是在科学领域，构建和更新基准测试需要大量的时间、劳动和专业知识，使得评估难以与智能体能力的进步保持一致。我们提出了AutoSciBench框架，能够自动生成和迭代调整科学智能体基准，确保评估与智能体能力的演变相匹配。通过对任务的高层概念和低层配方的定义，AutoSciBench能够在智能体解决任务的过程中不断优化基准，提升评估的有效性。

papers.title: Taming VLAs under Robot Execution Errors: Self-Compensation and Stress Testing
papers.abstract: Abstract  Vision-language-action (VLA) policies often fail when a robot's executed motion deviates from their commanded action. Such execution errors arise from the robot's mechanics and operating conditions, such as wear and payload changes. We propose self-compensating VLA, a deployment-time adaptation method that enables a VLA policy to pre-compensate for the robot's execution errors when generating commands. Without task rewards or labels, it updates the policy online using the residual between the action commanded by a VLA and the motion executed by the robot. To stress-test VLA robustness across execution conditions that are impractical to cover with physical robots alone, we introduce RoboStress, a controlled simulation benchmark. It combines established joint-level models of friction, backlash, compliance, and gravity-compensation error into seven deployment scenarios whose execution errors depend on the robot's state and motion history. On RoboStress, self-compensating VLA achieves higher average task success than both the base policies and methods that build in robustness during training. On two physical robot arms with different usage histories, it raises the average task success rate by more than 30 percentage points on each arm, and the gains extend to objects not seen in the task demonstrations.

ru.title: Адаптивная компенсация ошибок исполнения для политик зрение-язык-действие
ru.desc: В статье предлагается метод самокомпенсации для политик зрение-язык-действие (VLA), которые адаптируются во время развёртывания робота. Метод позволяет VLA политике предварительно компенсировать ошибки исполнения робота при генерировании команд, используя невязку между командным действием и реально исполненным движением, без необходимости в наградах или разметке. Авторы представили бенчмарк RoboStress для тестирования робастности VLA в различных условиях эксплуатации, объединяющий модели трения, люфта, деформации и ошибок гравитационной компенсации. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что самокомпенсирующаяся VLA повышает успешность выполнения задач на реальных робот-манипуляторах более чем на 30 процентных пункта.

en.title: Self-Compensating VLA: Adapting to Execution Errors in Real-Time
en.desc: This paper addresses the challenges faced by vision-language-action (VLA) policies when robots encounter execution errors during their tasks. The authors introduce a method called self-compensating VLA, which allows the robot to adjust its commands in real-time based on the difference between intended and actual movements. This adaptation occurs without needing additional task rewards or labels, as it learns from the discrepancies in execution. To evaluate the robustness of this approach, the researchers developed RoboStress, a simulation benchmark that tests VLA policies under various challenging conditions, demonstrating significant improvements in task success rates for physical robots.

zh.title: 自我补偿VLA：提升机器人执行精度的创新方法
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种自我补偿的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略，旨在解决机器人执行动作时的偏差问题。这种偏差通常是由于机器人的机械特性和操作条件引起的，例如磨损和负载变化。自我补偿VLA方法在生成指令时，能够在线更新策略，以补偿机器人执行中的误差，而无需依赖任务奖励或标签。通过引入RoboStress这一受控仿真基准，研究者能够在多种执行条件下测试VLA的鲁棒性，结果显示该方法在实际应用中显著提高了任务成功率。

papers.title: TRACE: Rollout-Guided Quantization-Aware Training for FP4 Reinforcement Learning of MoE Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract  Reinforcement learning (RL) for post-training large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial computation and memory overhead during rollout generation, which motivates low-precision rollout for efficient RL training. However, existing FP4 RL methods suffer from a key limitation: they primarily optimize quantization accuracy on the training and rollout paths independently rather than directly reducing the discrepancy between the two quantized execution paths. In this work, we propose TRACE (Train-Rollout Quantization Alignment via Compact GuidancE), an FP4 quantization framework for RL training of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models that addresses the limitation of existing FP4 RL methods. TRACE incorporates rollout-guided quantization-aware training that uses rollout-side quantization outcomes to guide training-side FP4 rounding decisions, directly reducing train-rollout discrepancy. Moreover, TRACE adopts an efficient quantization-information caching scheme that selectively retains mantissa and scale information from deeper layers to reduce the storage and communication overhead introduced by rollout guidance. We evaluate TRACE on four large-scale MoE language models across reasoning, coding, and long-horizon RL tasks. Our results demonstrate that TRACE enables joint FP4 weight/activation and FP4 KV-cache rollout with RL performance comparable to BF16 rollout, while achieving up to 5.4xrollout speedup and strong final FP4 performance compared with post-hoc FP4 quantization of BF16-trained policies.

ru.title: Синхронизация квантизации между обучением и инференсом для эффективного RL
ru.desc: Работа предлагает TRACE — фреймворк для низкоточной квантизации FP4 при обучении LLM методами reinforcement learning на моделях Mixture-of-Experts. Основная проблема заключается в том, что существующие методы оптимизируют точность квантизации на этапах обучения и инференса отдельно, что приводит к расхождению между ними. TRACE использует данные с этапа инференса для направления решений квантизации на этапе обучения, прямо сокращая этот discrepancy между двумя путями вычисления. Дополнительно предложена эффективная схема кэширования информации о квантизации, которая селективно сохраняет данные из глубоких слоев, снижая затраты памяти и связи при руководстве от rollout.

en.title: Aligning Training and Rollout for Efficient RL in Language Models
en.desc: This paper introduces TRACE, a new framework for improving reinforcement learning (RL) in large language models (LLMs) by using low-precision quantization. The main issue with existing methods is that they optimize the training and rollout processes separately, leading to discrepancies in performance. TRACE addresses this by aligning the quantization of training and rollout paths, using insights from the rollout to inform training decisions. The framework also includes a caching mechanism to efficiently manage quantization information, resulting in faster rollouts and comparable performance to higher precision methods.

zh.title: TRACE：高效的强化学习量化对齐框架
zh.desc: 本论文提出了一种名为TRACE的框架，用于提高大语言模型的强化学习训练效率。TRACE通过引入回滚引导的量化感知训练，直接减少训练和回滚路径之间的差异，从而优化量化精度。该方法还采用了一种高效的量化信息缓存方案，减少了存储和通信开销。实验结果表明，TRACE在多个任务上实现了与BF16回滚相当的强化学习性能，同时提高了回滚速度。

papers.title: HuatuoGPT-3: RL-Only Domain Adaptation from Base Models
papers.abstract: Abstract  Domain adaptation aims to turn a general-purpose large language model (LLM) into an expert for a target domain. While the dominant SFT+RL pipeline offers a convenient cold start, it may reduce exploration diversity and introduces additional complexity through multi-stage optimization. These limitations motivate RL-only adaptation. However, pure on-policy RL suffers from a cold-start problem, while mixed-policy RL still falls short: informative tokens in teacher outputs are learned too slowly in early training, and stale teacher outputs can hinder later improvement. We identify these two failure modes as Gradient Starvation and Teacher-Distribution Anchoring. To address them, we propose One-stage Policy Optimization (OnePO), which treats teacher outputs as transient guidance for policy improvement. OnePO combines Adaptive Objective Evolution to strengthen learning on informative low-probability teacher tokens and Teacher Retirement to discard teacher outputs once the current policy can surpass them. On medical adaptation, OnePO achieves 67.2 on HealthBench (Total) with only 20K training samples, outperforming SFT+RL and pure RL by 2.7 and 7.4 points, respectively. We further scale OnePO to produce HuatuoGPT-3, an open-source medical LLM series whose 27B variant reaches 70.1 on HealthBench (Total) and 71.4 on HealthBench Professional, surpassing frontier models such as GPT-6 Astra. Models and code are available at https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/HuatuoGPT-3.

ru.title: Однофазная оптимизация политики для экспертизации языковых моделей
ru.desc: В работе предлагается метод адаптации больших языковых моделей для специальных областей, использующий только обучение с подкреплением вместо традиционной двухэтапной схемы SFT+RL. Авторы выявили две ключевые проблемы: недостаточное обучение на информативных токенах с низкой вероятностью и негативное влияние устаревших выходов учителя на обучение. Предложенный метод OnePO решает эти проблемы через адаптивную эволюцию целевой функции и пенсионирование выходов учителя, когда текущая политика их превосходит. Метод достигает выдающихся результатов в медицинской адаптации, превосходя стандартные подходы и конкурирующие модели на бенчмарках HealthBench.

en.title: Transforming LLMs into Domain Experts with OnePO
en.desc: This paper discusses a method for adapting large language models (LLMs) to specific domains, particularly in the medical field. The authors highlight the limitations of traditional supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning (SFT+RL) approaches, which can lead to reduced exploration and complexity. They introduce One-stage Policy Optimization (OnePO), a novel technique that improves learning by treating teacher outputs as temporary guidance and enhancing the learning of rare but informative tokens. The results show that OnePO significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving high scores on medical benchmarks with fewer training samples.

zh.title: 单阶段策略优化：提升领域适应性的新方法
zh.desc: 领域适应旨在将通用的大型语言模型（LLM）转变为特定领域的专家。传统的SFT+RL方法虽然方便，但可能降低探索多样性，并增加多阶段优化的复杂性。为了解决这些问题，本文提出了一种新的单阶段策略优化方法（OnePO），通过将教师输出视为临时指导来改善策略学习。实验结果表明，OnePO在医疗领域的适应性上表现优异，超越了现有的SFT+RL和纯RL方法。

papers.title: World Action Learning via Interaction-Centric Spectral Latent Guidance
papers.abstract: Abstract  Learning general-purpose robot policies requires large-scale real-world interaction data, yet collecting robot demonstrations remains expensive and difficult to scale. Egocentric videos offer abundant human interaction experience with task-relevant semantics for robotic manipulation, but direct transfer is challenging for two reasons: latent actions inferred from frame reconstruction can be dominated by nuisance variation such as ego-camera motion, and human and robot behaviors often exhibit different temporal dynamics. We propose WING (World Action Learning via INteraction-Centric Spectral Latent Guidance), a framework for transferring interaction knowledge from egocentric videos to robot policies. WING first separates observer-induced motion from hand-object interaction and distills the interaction-centric component into latent actions. It then exploits the observation that cross-embodiment task semantics are concentrated in slowly varying temporal structures, identifying shared low-frequency components between egocentric latent actions and robot behaviors in the spectral domain and using them to guide action generation. WING achieves average success rates of 99.20% on LIBERO, 93.80% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 57.7% on RoboCasa-GR1, and also performs strongly across four real-world manipulation tasks under diverse generalization settings. These results show that interaction-centric spectral guidance provides an effective and scalable way to transfer physical interaction knowledge from human egocentric video to robot control. Project page: https://mikuz12.github.io/wing/
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Передача знаний о взаимодействии от человека к роботу через спектральный анализ
ru.desc: Статья описывает WING — фреймворк для передачи знаний о взаимодействии с объектами из эгоцентрических видео человека к политикам робота. Основной вызов заключается в том, что движение камеры и различия во временной динамике между человеком и роботом мешают прямой передаче. WING решает эту проблему, отделяя движение наблюдателя от взаимодействия рука-объект и используя спектральный анализ для выделения низкочастотных компонентов, общих для обоих типов агентов. Метод достигает высоких показателей успеха на нескольких бенчмарках и реальных задачах манипуляции роботом.

en.title: Transfer Human Interaction Knowledge to Robots with WING
en.desc: This paper introduces WING, a novel framework designed to help robots learn from human interactions captured in egocentric videos. The challenge lies in separating useful hand-object interactions from irrelevant camera movements and different behavior timings between humans and robots. WING addresses this by focusing on the slow-changing aspects of actions, allowing it to identify common patterns in both human and robot behaviors. The framework demonstrates impressive success rates in various robotic manipulation tasks, showcasing its potential for scalable knowledge transfer from human experiences to robotic control.

zh.title: 通过视频学习机器人交互知识的有效方法
zh.desc: 本论文提出了一种名为WING的框架，用于将人类在第一人称视频中的交互知识转移到机器人控制策略中。WING通过分离观察者引起的运动和手-物体交互，提取出与交互相关的潜在动作。该方法利用了跨身体任务语义在低频结构中的集中性，识别出人类和机器人行为之间的共享低频成分，以指导动作生成。实验结果表明，WING在多个真实世界的操作任务中表现出色，成功率高达99.20%。

papers.title: EVISKILL: Grounding Skill Evolution in Replayable Evidence
papers.abstract: Abstract  Continual skill evolution enables LLM agents to accumulate and refine reusable procedural knowledge from interaction experience without updating model parameters. Its effectiveness depends on determining not only what to change, but also why a change is justified and when it should become persistent guidance. However, existing experience-driven methods can lose the behavioral evidence and task contexts supporting edits. Moreover, a global validation outcome provides an incomplete judgment of its constituent changes: locally supported corrections may be discarded with a rejected revision, while evidence may require further experience to inform useful updates. To this end, we introduce EVISKILL, an evidence-driven framework that organizes execution observations into Replayable Evidence Cards and synthesizes edits with explicit links to their supporting contexts. Targeted replay verifies these edits through re-execution and provides feedback for correction. Across epochs, EVISKILL preserves evidence and provisionally retains supported edits for further refinement, while global validation governs their incorporation into the final skill. Experiments on three interactive benchmarks across six LLM backbones demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach.
affiliations: School of Artificial Intelligence, Jilin University, Changchun, China

ru.title: Знания из опыта: эволюция навыков агентов через сохранение свидетельств
ru.desc: Работа представляет EVISKILL — фреймворк для постоянного обучения агентов на основе больших языковых моделей, который позволяет накапливать и совершенствовать процедурные знания без обновления параметров модели. Ключевая идея заключается в сохранении и организации свидетельств из опыта взаимодействия в виде воспроизводимых карточек, которые явно связывают внесённые изменения с контекстом их обоснования. Фреймворк использует целевую переактивацию для проверки правок через переисполнение и собирает обратную связь для коррекции, постепенно накапливая подтверждённые изменения. Экспериментальная оценка на трёх интерактивных бенчмарках показывает эффективность подхода для различных LLM моделей.

en.title: EVISKILL: Evolving Skills with Evidence-Driven Learning
en.desc: The paper presents EVISKILL, a framework designed for continual skill evolution in large language model (LLM) agents. It focuses on how these agents can learn and refine their skills from past interactions without needing to change their underlying model parameters. EVISKILL organizes execution observations into Replayable Evidence Cards, which help in justifying and verifying changes made to the model's behavior. By using targeted replay for feedback and maintaining evidence for future updates, the framework ensures that useful edits are preserved and refined over time, leading to improved performance across various tasks.

zh.title: EVISKILL：证据驱动的持续技能演化框架
zh.desc: 本论文提出了一种名为EVISKILL的框架，用于持续技能演化，使大型语言模型（LLM）能够从交互经验中积累和精炼可重用的程序知识。该框架通过将执行观察组织成可重放的证据卡，确保编辑与其支持上下文之间的明确链接，从而避免现有方法中丢失行为证据和任务上下文的问题。EVISKILL通过重新执行验证这些编辑，并提供反馈以进行修正，同时在多个周期中保留证据并暂时保留支持的编辑，以便进一步优化。实验结果表明，该方法在六个LLM基础模型的三个交互基准上表现出色。

papers.title: Selection-Based Structured Reasoning: Toward Efficient Multimodal Search Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  Multimodal agents commonly generate free-form reasoning before each action. For small models, limited model capacity can result in lengthy reasoning that provides little useful guidance for action generation while incurring substantial inference cost. To address this challenge, we introduce Selection-based Structured Reasoning (SSR), a framework that reformulates reasoning as selection instead of open-ended generation. SSR represents recurring high-level reasoning as pre-specified, reusable natural-language candidates. At each turn, the model selects from these reasoning candidates based on their likelihoods given the current context, without requiring an auxiliary task head. Using pre-specified reasoning traces enables parallel scoring, where teacher-forced prefilling computes token likelihoods concurrently within and across candidates using a shared context KV cache. We evaluate SSR on seven multimodal search benchmarks using 2B and 4B models. Across multiple reinforcement learning objectives and supervised fine-tuning, SSR delivers significant efficiency gains without sacrificing task performance. SSR achieves an average success rate competitive with leading search agents of the same scale, while reducing per-turn reasoning latency by over 90% and total per-question model inference latency by 28-54%. Project page: https://zfy0314.github.io/ssr-webpage/.

ru.title: Быстрые рассуждения через структурированный выбор вместо свободной генерации
ru.desc: В этой работе предлагается новый подход Selection-based Structured Reasoning (SSR) для многомодальных агентов, который переформулирует задачу рассуждения как выбор между предопределёнными кандидатами вместо свободной генерации текста. Такой метод особенно полезен для маленьких моделей, так как позволяет избежать длинных и неинформативных рассуждений, которые замедляют инференс. Благодаря использованию параллельного скоринга с общим KV кэшем, SSR достигает снижения задержки рассуждения более чем на 90% и общей задержки инференса на 28-54%. При этом модель сохраняет конкурентную производительность на семи многомодальных бенчмарках, работая с моделями размером 2B и 4B параметров.

en.title: Efficient Reasoning through Selection in Multimodal Agents
en.desc: This paper presents a new framework called Selection-based Structured Reasoning (SSR) for multimodal agents that improves the efficiency of reasoning processes. Instead of generating reasoning from scratch, SSR uses pre-defined natural-language candidates that represent high-level reasoning. The model selects the most relevant reasoning candidate based on the current context, which allows for faster processing and reduced inference costs. The results show that SSR significantly enhances performance on multimodal search tasks while decreasing reasoning latency by over 90%.

zh.title: 选择性推理，提升多模态智能体效率
zh.desc: 多模态智能体通常在每个动作之前生成自由形式的推理。对于小型模型，有限的模型容量可能导致冗长的推理，提供的指导有限，同时增加推理成本。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了基于选择的结构化推理（SSR）框架，将推理重新定义为选择而不是开放式生成。SSR通过预先指定的可重用自然语言候选项来表示重复的高层推理，从而在多个多模态搜索基准上实现了显著的效率提升。

papers.title: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
papers.abstract: Abstract  The executable harness surrounding a GUI model determines how observations are assembled, actions are executed, and verification, recovery, and termination are controlled. Compared with harness optimization for non-GUI agents, automatically optimizing this harness poses three coupled challenges: reconciling model intent with observed visual effects, diagnosing failures under variable execution outcomes, and identifying recurrent failure patterns across tasks and translating them into reusable runtime changes. We introduce GUI-HARVEST, an automatic harness optimizer that enables self-improving GUI agents with frozen backbone models. First, to ground diagnosis in observed action effects, it aligns model outputs and executed actions with before-and-after screenshots, tying findings to specific interface transitions. Second, to account for execution variability, it treats repeated runs of the same task as a joint evidence unit, using within-task comparisons to locate outcome-relevant behavioral differences. Third, it consolidates verified findings across tasks into recurring failure patterns, maps them to bounded source-code edits with predictions recorded before evaluation, and checks the predicted behavioral effects alongside task performance through repeated execution. Experiments on OSWorld-Verified show consistent held-out gains across six general-purpose open, GUI-specialized open, and proprietary backbone models; Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct gains 12.33 points on the full suite. Frozen-harness transfer improves GPT-5 by 13.87 percentage points on WindowsAgentArena at 50 steps without further optimization. With the same backbone and initial harness, GUI-HARVEST outperforms Self-Harness and Meta-Harness, suggesting that GUI-specific diagnosis and validation help harness improvements generalize to unseen tasks. The code is available at https://github.com/GaryYang12345/GUI-HARVEST.
affiliations: Shenzhen Research Institute of Big Data
The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

ru.title: Самосовершенствующиеся GUI-агенты через автоматическую оптимизацию обвязки
ru.desc: В статье предлагается GUI-HARVEST — система автоматической оптимизации обвязки (harness) для агентов, взаимодействующих с графическим интерфейсом, при сохранении неизменной основной модели. Метод решает три ключевые задачи: согласование намерений модели с визуальными эффектами на экране путём анализа скриншотов до и после действий, диагностирование сбоев с учётом вариативности выполнения через сравнение повторных прогонов одной задачи, и выявление рецидивирующих паттернов ошибок с их преобразованием в переиспользуемые изменения в коде. Экспериментальные результаты на наборе OSWorld-Verified показывают устойчивое улучшение производительности различных моделей-бэкбонов, включая перенос оптимизированной обвязки на новые задачи и модели, что демонстрирует эффективность GUI-специфичной диагностики и валидации.

en.title: Optimizing GUI Agents for Better Performance with GUI-HARVEST
en.desc: The paper presents GUI-HARVEST, an automatic optimizer for harnessing GUI models, which enhances the performance of self-improving GUI agents. It addresses three main challenges: aligning model outputs with visual effects, diagnosing failures from variable execution outcomes, and identifying recurring failure patterns for runtime improvements. By using before-and-after screenshots and treating repeated task runs as evidence units, it effectively diagnoses and improves GUI interactions. The results show significant performance gains across various models, indicating that GUI-specific optimizations lead to better generalization in unseen tasks.

zh.title: GUI-HARVEST：提升图形用户界面代理的自动优化工具
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为GUI-HARVEST的自动化工具，用于优化图形用户界面（GUI）模型的执行环境。该工具解决了三个主要挑战：将模型意图与观察到的视觉效果对齐、在不同执行结果下诊断失败，以及识别任务中的重复失败模式并将其转化为可重用的运行时更改。通过对执行动作的效果进行对比分析，GUI-HARVEST能够提高GUI代理的自我改进能力，并在多个模型上实现了显著的性能提升。实验结果表明，该方法在不同的任务和模型上均表现出色，验证了GUI特定的诊断和验证对优化的有效性。

papers.title: EmbodiedSmith: Scaling Embodied Data through Recursive Self-Improvement Flywheel in Simulation
papers.abstract: Abstract  Scaling robotic foundation models requires diverse training data and reliable evaluation environments. Simulation offers a scalable solution, yet existing generation pipelines remain constrained by predefined assets and skills, a disconnect between scene generation and task generation, and limited support for complex embodiments and physics. We introduce EmbodiedSmith, a framework for scalable embodied data generation through recursive self-improvement (RSI). EmbodiedSmith unifies asset, scene, and task generation in a pipeline that supports autonomous creation and language-driven customization. Its core is an agentic refinement loop: scene generation anticipates downstream task requirements, while task generation guides targeted scene edits, allowing scenes and tasks to iteratively improve one another. This joint refinement improves task generation success, including for long-horizon tasks. The framework further supports mobile manipulators, humanoids, and dexterous hands, as well as interactions involving deformable objects and fluids, broadening the range of behaviors and physical phenomena represented in generated data. Together, these capabilities provide a flexible simulation engine for both robot pretraining and evaluation. Extensive experiments validate the quality, diversity, and generation efficiency of the resulting data, while downstream policy experiments demonstrate that increased data diversity improves generalization.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

ru.title: Самоулучшающаяся симуляция для предварительного обучения роботов
ru.desc: В статье представлена платформа EmbodiedSmith для масштабируемой генерации тренировочных данных роботов через рекурсивное самоулучшение. Система объединяет генерацию активов, сцен и задач в единый конвейер, где сцены и задачи итеративно улучшают друг друга через агентный цикл уточнения. Платформа поддерживает разнообразные робототехнические системы: мобильные манипуляторы, гуманоиды и ловкие манипуляторы, а также взаимодействие с деформируемыми объектами и жидкостями. Экспериментальная валидация показывает, что увеличенное разнообразие синтетических данных значительно улучшает обобщение обученных политик управления.

en.title: Empowering Robots with Self-Improving Simulation Data
en.desc: This paper presents EmbodiedSmith, a novel framework designed to enhance the generation of training data for robotic foundation models. It addresses limitations in existing simulation pipelines by integrating asset, scene, and task generation into a cohesive system that allows for recursive self-improvement. The framework enables autonomous scene creation and customization through language, facilitating a feedback loop where scene and task generation mutually enhance each other. Extensive experiments show that this approach not only improves the quality and diversity of generated data but also enhances the generalization capabilities of robotic policies in complex tasks.

zh.title: 智能化数据生成，提升机器人能力
zh.desc: 本文介绍了EmbodiedSmith框架，它通过递归自我改进（RSI）实现可扩展的机器人数据生成。该框架将资产、场景和任务生成统一在一个管道中，支持自主创建和基于语言的定制。其核心是一个智能化的优化循环，场景生成能够预见下游任务需求，而任务生成则指导场景的有针对性编辑，从而实现场景和任务的相互改进。通过广泛的实验验证，结果显示生成的数据在质量、多样性和生成效率上都有显著提升，且数据多样性提高了模型的泛化能力。

papers.title: DiVeR: Decision-Critical Verifier Learning for VLA Test-Time Scaling
papers.abstract: Abstract  Scaling robot data and model capacity has improved Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, but further progress is constrained by the high cost of robotic data. Verifier-guided test-time scaling offers an efficient alternative by sampling multiple action candidates and selecting the one most likely to lead to task success at inference time. Existing classification-based verifiers learn from trajectory-level outcomes but treat all visited states equally, even though their value for candidate discrimination can vary across a trajectory. At many states, plausible actions are similar and provide limited discrimination signal, while only a sparse set of decision-critical states admits meaningfully different actions that can substantially affect downstream outcomes. To address this, we propose DiVeR, which estimates decision criticality from the dispersion of sampled action representations. DiVeR then uses this signal to reweight verifier learning toward states where action selection is most consequential, without requiring step-level annotations or additional environment interaction. Across LIBERO, RoboCasa, and real-world experiments on a Franka Research 3 robot, DiVeR consistently improves task success through more effective verifier-guided action selection, while adding negligible verifier inference overhead.

ru.title: Умный выбор действий через оценку критичности состояний
ru.desc: Статья представляет DiVeR — метод для улучшения политик робот-зрение-язык-действие (VLA) за счёт эффективного масштабирования на этапе тестирования. Авторы предлагают использовать верификатор, который выбирает оптимальное действие из нескольких кандидатов, основываясь на оценке вероятности успеха задачи. Ключевая идея заключается в определении критичности каждого состояния по дисперсии представлений действий: на одних шагах действия похожи и мало помогают выбору, а на других — они существенно различаются и влияют на исход. DiVeR перевешивает обучение верификатора в сторону критичных состояний, не требуя дополнительных аннотаций или взаимодействия со средой.

en.title: Enhancing Robot Action Selection with Decision-Critical Insights
en.desc: This paper introduces DiVeR, a method that enhances Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies by improving the selection of actions during robot tasks. It addresses the challenge of high costs associated with robotic data by using verifier-guided test-time scaling, which samples multiple action candidates and selects the most promising one. DiVeR focuses on identifying decision-critical states in a trajectory, where the choice of action significantly impacts the outcome, rather than treating all states equally. The method has been shown to improve task success rates in various robotic environments without requiring additional data collection or complex annotations.

zh.title: 提升机器人任务成功率的新方法
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为DiVeR的方法，用于提高机器人在视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略中的任务成功率。该方法通过评估采样动作表示的分散程度来估计决策的关键性，从而在验证器学习中重新加权，关注那些对动作选择影响最大的状态。与传统的基于分类的验证器不同，DiVeR不需要逐步注释或额外的环境交互，能够有效地选择最有可能成功的动作。实验结果表明，DiVeR在多个机器人平台上均显著提高了任务成功率，同时对验证器推理的开销几乎可以忽略不计。

papers.title: Making LLMs Say What They Think: Measuring and Improving CoT-Interpretability Alignment
papers.abstract: Abstract  Chain-of-thought (CoT) traces often serve as a proxy for how Large Language Models (LLMs) arrive at their answers. However, growing evidence shows that models' CoT often fails to reflect their internal computations and can be changed without affecting their final answers. In this work, we measure and improve the alignment between the reasoning described in an LLM's CoT and what it computes internally. We propose CoT-Interpretability Alignment (CIA), a metric that measures the agreement between a model's CoT traces and its internal reasoning strategies as detected by interpretability tools. We evaluate CIA on three tasks (two-hop question answering, hint intervention, and integer multiplication) across three LLMs, finding that LLMs exhibit limited alignment across all tasks (44.8-75.9%). We then experiment with improving CIA via post-training, setting both the task accuracy and parametric faithfulness signals as a reward. Experiments show that we can substantially improve CoT parametric faithfulness while maintaining or improving the task accuracy. We provide rich analysis, such as their generalization patterns. Our work provides both a framework for auditing CoT parametric faithfulness and a pathway toward making models' explicit reasoning more trustworthy. Code and data are available at https://github.com/yihuaihong/CIA-minimal-repro.

ru.title: Синхронизация видимых рассуждений языковых моделей с их внутренними вычислениями
ru.desc: В этой работе исследуется проблема несоответствия между цепочкой рассуждений (Chain-of-Thought), которую генерирует большая языковая модель, и её действительными внутренними вычислениями. Авторы предлагают метрику CoT-Interpretability Alignment (CIA), которая измеряет согласованность между явными рассуждениями модели и её реальными стратегиями обработки информации, выявленными с помощью инструментов интерпретируемости. Эксперименты показали, что современные LLM демонстрируют низкое выравнивание (44.8-75.9%) на различных задачах, и авторы предлагают метод постобучения с использованием сигналов качества и параметрической верности для улучшения этого показателя. Работа предоставляет как инструмент для аудита надёжности рассуждений LLM, так и способы повышения доверия к явным рассуждениям моделей.

en.title: Aligning Reasoning: Enhancing Trust in LLMs' Chain-of-Thought
en.desc: This paper investigates the relationship between the chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning of Large Language Models (LLMs) and their internal computations. It introduces a new metric called CoT-Interpretability Alignment (CIA) to measure how well the CoT aligns with the model's actual reasoning processes. The authors find that there is often a significant misalignment between CoT and internal reasoning across various tasks. They propose methods to improve this alignment while maintaining task accuracy, ultimately aiming to enhance the trustworthiness of LLMs' reasoning capabilities.

zh.title: 提升模型推理可信度的关键
zh.desc: 本文探讨了大型语言模型（LLMs）在回答问题时的推理过程，特别是链式思维（CoT）与模型内部计算之间的关系。研究发现，CoT并不总能准确反映模型的内部推理，且可以在不影响最终答案的情况下进行修改。为此，提出了链式思维可解释性对齐（CIA）指标，用于衡量CoT与内部推理策略之间的一致性。通过后训练实验，研究表明可以显著提高CoT的参数可信度，同时保持或提高任务准确性。

papers.title: Understanding and Enhancing Backdoor Persistency in LLM Agent Post-Training
papers.abstract: Abstract  Developers can build LLM agents by adapting third-party models through benign post-training. We study a supply-chain threat in which an attacker supplies a model with a backdoor: hidden behavior that produces malicious outputs when a particular input pattern appears. Focusing on software-engineering agents, we ask whether such backdoors survive the developer's supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and subsequent task-level reinforcement learning (RL). We observe that benign SFT substantially reduces attack success, but subsequent RL often preserves the residual behavior and sometimes even increases attack success. Our analysis of backdoor erosion during SFT identifies two factors that may favor survival: initial backdoor strength and gradient compatibility with benign training. These factors motivate PersistBD, which refines an already-backdoored model before release to improve its persistency through the benign post-training process. On Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, PersistBD raises attack success from 20% to 74% after SFT and from 20% to 76% after SFT-RL, while maintaining comparable benign task performance. Together, our results show that backdoors can remain active through benign post-training and that adversaries can deliberately increase their persistence. This highlights a supply-chain risk for AI developers and motivates stronger techniques for detecting and mitigating inherited backdoors when adapting third-party models into agents. Our code is available at https://github.com/uiuc-kang-lab/PersistBD.

ru.title: Скрытые угрозы в адаптированных моделях: как бэкдоры выживают при обучении
ru.desc: В статье исследуется уязвимость supply-chain для LLM агентов, где злоумышленник внедряет скрытое вредоносное поведение (backdoor) в предварительно обученную модель. Авторы показывают, что хотя стандартное supervised fine-tuning (SFT) снижает эффективность атаки, последующее reinforcement learning (RL) часто сохраняет остаточное вредоносное поведение и даже усиливает его. Исследование выявляет два фактора, влияющих на сохранение backdoor: начальная сила backdoor и совместимость градиентов с доброкачественной обучающей выборкой. На основе этих выводов предложен метод PersistBD, который делает backdoor более устойчивым к post-training процессу, увеличивая успешность атаки с 20% до 74-76% на модели Qwen2.5-Coder-7B.

en.title: Backdoor Persistence: A Hidden Threat in AI Model Training
en.desc: This paper investigates the risks of backdoor attacks in large language model (LLM) agents, particularly during the process of benign post-training. It finds that while supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can reduce the effectiveness of these backdoors, subsequent reinforcement learning (RL) may inadvertently preserve or even enhance their malicious capabilities. The authors introduce a method called PersistBD, which aims to refine backdoored models to ensure their persistence through benign training processes. Their experiments demonstrate a significant increase in attack success rates, raising concerns about supply-chain vulnerabilities in AI development and the need for improved detection methods.

zh.title: 后门攻击的持久性与防范
zh.desc: 本文研究了在软件工程代理中，攻击者如何通过后门攻击影响模型的输出。我们发现，虽然良性的监督微调（SFT）可以显著降低攻击成功率，但后续的强化学习（RL）可能会保留残余的后门行为，甚至提高攻击成功率。我们提出了PersistBD方法，通过在发布前对已经存在后门的模型进行精炼，增强其在良性后训练过程中的持久性。我们的实验结果表明，后门可以在良性后训练中保持活跃，这对AI开发者构成了供应链风险。

papers.title: Hiding Tool Latency in On-Device Cascaded Voice Agent through Speculative Execution
papers.abstract: Abstract  Tool-augmented speech assistants typically serialize automatic speech recognition, large language model inference, and external tool execution. As a result, tool latency is incurred only after the user has finished speaking and the LLM has identified the required tool calls. We present speculative tool execution for on-device cascaded voice agents, which predicts tool requests from partial ASR hypotheses and initiates tool execution while speech is still being received, thereby reducing end-to-end response latency. Our approach introduces a Predictor module that anticipates tool calls during speech recognition, executes them speculatively, and caches the results. The cached outputs are then injected into the LLM prompt, enabling faster responses. Additionally, to mitigate errors caused by user self-corrections during speech, we employ a rule-based validation mechanism that selectively injects only valid cached results. As a final safeguard, the LLM retains the ability to issue tool calls directly, ensuring that the latency of our framework is upper-bounded by the baseline serial execution pipeline in the worst case. We evaluate our method using live measurements from a fully implemented Android voice assistant. Our approach reduces the median time-to-first-audio from 5.79,s to 4.60,s and decreases the standard deviation from 3.49,s to 2.81,s, resulting in more predictable response latency.

ru.title: Предсказание и параллельное выполнение инструментов для ускорения голосовых ассистентов
ru.desc: В работе представлен метод спекулятивного выполнения инструментов для голосовых ассистентов, который предсказывает запросы к внешним сервисам на основе частичных гипотез автоматического распознавания речи и инициирует их выполнение ещё во время произнесения пользователем текста. Модуль-предиктор предугадывает необходимые вызовы инструментов во время распознавания и кэширует их результаты для последующей инъекции в подсказку LLM. Для повышения надёжности используется валидационный механизм, который отбирает только корректные кэшированные результаты и игнорирует самоисправления пользователя. Система гарантирует, что в худшем случае производительность не хуже, чем при последовательном выполнении, а на практике снижает время первого ответа с 5,79 до 4,60 секунд.

en.title: Speeding Up Speech Assistants with Speculative Tool Execution
en.desc: This paper introduces a new method for improving the speed of tool-augmented speech assistants by using speculative tool execution. Instead of waiting for the user to finish speaking before executing tool requests, the system predicts these requests during speech recognition. A Predictor module is used to anticipate and execute tool calls early, caching the results for faster access. The approach also includes a validation mechanism to ensure that only correct results are used, while still allowing the language model to make direct tool calls if needed, ultimately reducing response latency.

zh.title: 推测性工具执行，提升语音助手响应速度
zh.desc: 本论文提出了一种新的工具增强语音助手方法，称为推测性工具执行。该方法通过预测用户在说话时可能需要的工具请求，提前启动工具执行，从而减少响应延迟。我们引入了一个预测模块，在语音识别过程中预测工具调用，并缓存结果，以便快速响应。通过这种方式，我们的系统在实际应用中显著提高了语音助手的响应速度和可预测性。

papers.title: ALIVE: Interaction-Aligned Object Insertion for First-Frame-Guided Video Editing
papers.abstract: Abstract  Current video editors can insert objects but often struggle to make them participate in interactions such as being picked up or manipulated. We introduce ALIVE, a framework that makes inserted objects "alive" through coherent interactions with the source video's contents, using an edited first frame and an instruction naming only the added object. We curate 35,800 editing pairs combining 3D-rendered, model-generated, and real-world videos with general editing pairs from ROSE. Each pair differs in the target object's presence while preserving the surrounding action, teaching editors coordinated object behavior and source preservation. We further train a vision-language model (VLM) to predict interaction guidance from the same inputs. We introduce the ALIVE-interaction benchmark to assess interaction fidelity, source preservation, and visual coherence using a unified VLM-based protocol, and evaluate on the general video object insertion benchmark. Without VLM guidance, ALIVE improves Overall over the strongest evaluated baseline by 43.9% and 4.4% on the two benchmarks, respectively. VLM-predicted guidance further improves the ALIVE-interaction score by 0.95 points without additional user inputs.

ru.title: Оживляем вставленные объекты: согласованное взаимодействие в видеоредактировании
ru.desc: Представлена система ALIVE для естественного встраивания объектов в видеоредактирование с их реалистичным взаимодействием с окружением. Авторы собрали датасет из 35,800 пар видео, содержащих трёхмерную графику, синтетические видео и реальные сцены, где целевой объект взаимодействует с исходным контентом. Модель обучается предсказывать инструкции взаимодействия, используя видение-языковую модель (VLM) для понимания сцены. Система достигла значительного улучшения на 43.9% в метриках качества взаимодействия и сохранения исходного видео по сравнению с базовыми методами.

en.title: Bringing Video Objects to Life with ALIVE
en.desc: The paper presents ALIVE, a framework designed to enhance video editing by enabling inserted objects to interact naturally with their environment. It utilizes a combination of edited frames and specific instructions to create coherent interactions between the added objects and the original video content. The authors curated a large dataset of 35,800 editing pairs to train a vision-language model (VLM) that predicts how these objects should behave in context. The framework significantly improves interaction fidelity and visual coherence, outperforming existing methods by a notable margin, especially when guided by the VLM.

zh.title: 让视频中的对象“活起来”
zh.desc: 当前的视频编辑工具可以插入对象，但在使这些对象参与交互方面存在困难。我们提出了ALIVE框架，使插入的对象能够通过与源视频内容的连贯交互变得“活跃”。我们收集了35800对编辑样本，结合了3D渲染、模型生成和真实世界视频，帮助编辑者学习协调的对象行为和源内容的保留。通过训练视觉-语言模型（VLM），我们能够从相同的输入中预测交互指导，从而提升了交互的真实感和视觉一致性。

papers.title: AdvSim2Real : Training Web Agents Against Adaptive Prompt Injection in a Web World Model
papers.abstract: Abstract  Web agents complete user requests by reading and acting on pages that third parties write, so an instruction planted on a page can redirect the agent away from the user's goal. The agent cannot simply ignore the page, because the page also holds the values and controls the task requires. Current defenses fine-tune the agent on injections fixed before training, and attackers that adapt to the trained model bypass them. Adversarial training lets the attacker adapt but keeps the tasks fixed, so a task stops teaching once the agent solves it. We introduce AdvSim2Real, which co-evolves a task curriculum, an injection adversary, and the agent inside a frozen web world model. The curriculum is rewarded for tasks the agent solves about half of the time, and the adversary only for a success flip, an injection that turns a judged success into a failure. Training in the simulator makes a 4B agent both more capable and more robust: its completion rises with and without attacks, holds against a frontier-model adversary it never trained against, and its capability gain carries over to a real browser. On 150 web tasks, AdvSim2Real raises completion under this unseen adversary by 33.6\% relative to the base agent.
affiliations: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

ru.title: Устойчивость веб-агентов через адаптивное состязательное обучение в симуляции
ru.desc: В работе решается проблема защиты веб-агентов от злонамеренных инъекций, которые могут отвлечь модель от цели пользователя. Авторы предлагают AdvSim2Real — метод совместного обучения, который одновременно развивает curriculum обучающих задач, адаптивного противника и самого агента в замороженной модели веб-среды. Метод использует симуляцию для обучения, где curriculum вознаграждается за задачи средней сложности, а противник — за успешные атаки, которые превращают успех в неудачу. Экспериментально показано, что 4B параметр агент становится одновременно способнее и устойчивее к атакам, улучшая результаты даже против ненаученного противника на реальном браузере с относительным приростом 33.6%.

en.title: Enhancing Web Agents with AdvSim2Real: Robustness through Co-evolution
en.desc: This paper presents AdvSim2Real, a novel approach to enhance the robustness of web agents against adversarial injections while they perform tasks. It introduces a co-evolutionary training framework that simultaneously develops a task curriculum, an adversarial injection model, and the agent itself within a simulated web environment. The training rewards the agent for solving tasks and penalizes it when an adversary successfully alters a task's outcome. As a result, the trained agent shows significant improvements in task completion rates, even when faced with unseen adversarial strategies, demonstrating its effectiveness in real-world applications.

zh.title: 提升网络代理鲁棒性的创新训练方法
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种新的训练方法AdvSim2Real，用于提高网络代理在面对恶意注入时的鲁棒性。该方法通过共同演化任务课程、注入对手和代理，来增强代理的能力。与传统方法不同，AdvSim2Real在模拟环境中进行训练，使代理在未见过的对手面前也能提高完成率。实验结果表明，该方法在150个网络任务中，相较于基础代理，完成率提高了33.6%。

papers.title: Attacca: Goal-Directed Control under State Continuity for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  A central capability of embodied agents is to accomplish complex objectives through sequences of interdependent tasks. Yet existing visual goal-conditioned policies underlying these agents are typically evaluated on isolated interactions where the target is already visible, and thus do not capture the conditions that arise during continuous long-horizon task execution. In such settings, each task begins from the state left by the previous one: the agent may end at a different position and orientation, the world may have been modified, and the next interaction target may lie outside the current field of view. As a result, agents relying on such policies may struggle to proceed to the next task when they cannot ground their target in the current observation. To address this challenge, we propose Attacca, a new approach that trains visual goal-conditioned policies on complete search-to-interact trajectories using goal images decoupled from the execution environment. Attacca uses context-decoupled goal sampling to pair each demonstration with a class-compatible masked goal image from another world, removing direct scene and pose correspondence. It learns dense current-view grounding through a target-mask prediction head, providing auxiliary supervision beyond action imitation. We further introduce behavioral-phase conditioning that teaches the policy to distinguish Search, Approach, and Interact stages and adapt its control as execution progresses. We evaluate Attacca on multiple short- and long-horizon embodied tasks in Minecraft. Our method achieves 39.0-47.5% clean success, improving over the strongest baseline by 1.7-2.4x. On long-horizon tasks, it attains 54%, 30%, and 28% completion, yielding up to a 7x improvement.

ru.title: Поиск и взаимодействие: обучение агентов с развязанными целевыми образами
ru.desc: В работе предложен метод Attacca для обучения визуально-управляемых политик агентов, которые должны выполнять сложные многошаговые задачи в реальных условиях. Основная идея заключается в использовании целевых изображений, отделённых от окружения выполнения, и контекстно-развязанной выборки целей для улучшения обобщения. Модель обучается предсказывать маски целевых объектов и различать три фазы поведения: поиск, приближение и взаимодействие. Эксперименты в Minecraft показывают значительное улучшение - до 7x по сравнению с базовыми методами на долгосрочных задачах.

en.title: Empowering Agents with Context-Aware Goal Learning
en.desc: This paper introduces Attacca, a novel approach for training visual goal-conditioned policies in embodied agents. Unlike traditional methods that evaluate agents in isolated scenarios, Attacca focuses on continuous task execution where the agent must adapt to changing environments and targets. It employs context-decoupled goal sampling to enhance learning by using goal images that are not tied to the current scene, allowing for better generalization. Additionally, Attacca incorporates behavioral-phase conditioning to help the agent recognize different stages of task execution, significantly improving performance on both short- and long-horizon tasks in Minecraft.

zh.title: Attacca：提升复杂任务执行的智能体策略
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为Attacca的新方法，旨在训练视觉目标条件策略，以应对复杂的任务执行。与传统方法不同，Attacca通过使用与执行环境解耦的目标图像，来进行完整的搜索-交互轨迹训练。该方法引入了行为阶段条件，使得策略能够区分搜索、接近和交互阶段，从而在执行过程中自适应控制。实验结果表明，Attacca在Minecraft中的多项短期和长期任务上表现优异，成功率显著提高。

papers.title: Personal-Agent Mediated Recommendation with Cross-Platform User History
papers.abstract: Abstract  Modern recommendation is shifting from platform-centric personalization toward user-governed personalization, where a personal LLM agent can act on the user's behalf across services. We formalize this emerging paradigm as Personal-Agent Mediated Recommendation: a platform recommender ranks a candidate set using platform-local information, and a personal agent uses user-authorized cross-platform history to mediate the resulting ranking and produce the final top-K slate. Such mediation is nontrivial: the platform ranking can encode strong population evidence that the personal agent cannot observe, so effective mediation must therefore balance beneficial rescues against harmful overrides. To study this trade-off, we introduce MediateRec, a benchmark that includes scalable proxy cross-platform environments and a real cross-platform test under a controlled platform-agent information boundary. To train the agent to use cross-platform history effectively, we further propose Personal Attribution Mediation Optimization (PAMO), which counterfactually masks that history to estimate personal mediation support and reallocates rank-aware advantage mass under a platform-relative value floor. We theoretically prove that PAMO preserves cutoff-level advantage mass and is locally optimal among first-order reallocations that preserve this mass without lowering average platform-relative value. Experiments on MediateRec show that personal-agent mediation enables meaningful platform corrections, yet even strong proprietary LLMs introduce non-negligible harmful overrides. PAMO consistently improves over matched outcome-only RL across seen and unseen target platforms and on the real cross-platform test, while achieving a better rescue-harm balance.

ru.title: Балансировка персональных предпочтений и популярности в кросс-платформной рекомендации
ru.desc: В статье представляется новая парадигма рекомендации, где персональный LLM-агент действует от имени пользователя и переранжирует рекомендации платформы, используя историю пользователя из разных сервисов. Авторы формализуют эту задачу как медиирующую рекомендацию, где нужно балансировать между полезными корректировками рейтинга и вредными переопределениями, которые идут вразрез с популярными трендами платформы. Для исследования этого компромисса предложены бенчмарк MediateRec с симуляциями и реальный тест, а также метод PAMO, который использует контрфактические маски для оценки поддержки персональной медиации и переаллокации преимуществ ранга. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что PAMO эффективнее базовых методов обучения с подкреплением и лучше балансирует между полезными и вредными переопределениями рейтинга.

en.title: Empowering Users with Personal-Agent Mediated Recommendations
en.desc: This paper introduces a new approach to recommendation systems called Personal-Agent Mediated Recommendation, where a personal agent helps users make better choices across different platforms. The agent uses both platform-specific data and user-approved cross-platform history to refine recommendations, balancing the need to correct platform biases while avoiding harmful overrides. The authors present a benchmark called MediateRec to evaluate this approach and propose a method called Personal Attribution Mediation Optimization (PAMO) to enhance the agent's decision-making. Experiments show that PAMO improves the quality of recommendations by effectively managing the trade-off between beneficial corrections and harmful overrides.

zh.title: 用户主导的个性化推荐新范式
zh.desc: 现代推荐系统正从以平台为中心的个性化转向用户主导的个性化。在这种新兴范式中，个人代理可以代表用户在多个服务中进行操作。我们提出了个人代理中介推荐的概念，平台推荐系统使用平台本地信息对候选集进行排名，而个人代理则利用用户授权的跨平台历史来调整最终的推荐结果。为了有效地训练代理使用跨平台历史，我们提出了个人归因中介优化（PAMO），该方法在保持平台相对价值的基础上，优化了推荐的平衡。

papers.title: HiPLEX: Hierarchical Policy Factorization for Full Duplex Speech Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract  As human--AI interactions become more conversational, full-duplex speech language models capable of natural real-time dialogue are growing in importance. Beyond generating appropriate responses, these models must coordinate turn-taking, backchanneling, and floor management in real time. Reinforcement learning (RL) provides a way to refine these behaviors through direct feedback on interaction outcomes. However, existing RL methods either apply timing feedback to a token policy or optimize semantic content, leaving the joint improvement of timing and content unresolved. We introduce HiPLEX, an RL framework that factorizes a pretrained full-duplex text policy into a control policy that decides when to emit content and a conditional content policy that decides what to emit. The first factor selects among 'pad', 'epad', and 'con'. The second selects a token only when 'con' is chosen. This hierarchy describes conditional actions within each frame and uses the model's existing text head. We route timing advantages to the token-group factor through event-causal masks derived from generated speech episodes, and route an LLM-judge semantic advantage to the conditional content factor. Across three Moshi seeds on Full-Duplex-Bench v1, HiPLEX reduces takeover rates during natural user pauses and backchannel opportunities, and shortens post-interruption response latency relative to GRPO, while maintaining comparable judged interruption-response quality. On Moshi and PersonaPlex, HiPLEX better matches pooled human turn-timing and backchannel-rate marginals than GRPO.

ru.title: Иерархическая политика для синхронизации времени и содержимого в диалоговых языковых моделях
ru.desc: В работе предложен HiPLEX — фреймворк глубокого обучения с подкреплением для улучшения полнодуплексных речевых языковых моделей в естественном диалоге. Метод факторизирует предварительно обученную политику на две компоненты: управляющую политику, которая определяет, когда издавать содержимое (pad, epad или con), и условную политику содержимого, которая выбирает токены при активации con. Обратная связь маршрутизируется через событийно-причинные маски для улучшения временного согласования и LLM-судьи для оптимизации семантического качества. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что HiPLEX снижает частоту захватов очереди, улучшает обработку прерываний и лучше соответствует человеческим паттернам разговора по сравнению с базовыми методами.

en.title: Enhancing Conversational AI with HiPLEX: Timing Meets Content
en.desc: This paper presents HiPLEX, a reinforcement learning framework designed to enhance full-duplex speech language models for more natural human-AI conversations. HiPLEX separates the decision-making process into two policies: a control policy that manages when to speak and a content policy that determines what to say. By using event-causal masks and leveraging feedback from a large language model, HiPLEX improves timing and content generation simultaneously. The results show that HiPLEX effectively reduces interruptions and improves response timing compared to existing methods, while maintaining high-quality interactions.

zh.title: 优化人机对话的全双工模型
zh.desc: 随着人机交互变得更加对话化，能够进行自然实时对话的全双工语音语言模型变得越来越重要。这些模型不仅需要生成合适的回应，还必须实时协调轮流发言、反馈和管理发言权。我们提出了HiPLEX，这是一个强化学习框架，通过将预训练的全双工文本策略分解为控制策略和条件内容策略，来优化发言时机和内容的联合改进。实验结果表明，HiPLEX在自然用户暂停和反馈机会期间减少了接管率，并缩短了中断后的响应延迟，同时保持了与现有方法相当的响应质量。

papers.title: HLA: Expressive Hybrid Linear Attention via Chunk-Wise Dynamic Mixing
papers.abstract: Abstract  Linear attention enables efficient long-context autoregressive decoding by compressing history into recurrent states, but this compression can make selective access to sparse and distant information difficult. Existing chunk-based extensions increase memory capacity, yet learned chunk-mixing coefficients may remain fixed with respect to input content and therefore cannot adapt historical access to each query. We introduce Hybrid Linear Attention (HLA), a query-dependent chunk-level attention mechanism for Gated DeltaNet (GDN). HLA represents each completed chunk as an exact affine state transition and computes content-dependent routing gates from compact, self-attentively pooled representatives. Each gate interpolates the corresponding historical transition with the identity map, controlling both the chunk's additive memory and its transformation of earlier states. Effective-support regularization further encourages concentrated routing for sparse inference. We evaluate HLA under both pretrained adaptation and from-scratch training. Across Qwen3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B, HLA consistently improves over native GDN and fixed chunk mixing, with gains of up to 5.57 percentage points on LongBench-V2 and 3.97 points on RULER. In a controlled from-scratch 1.3B setting trained for 100B tokens with a 4K context, HLA also improves RULER performance from 4K to 32K, with gains increasing from 0.83 points at 4K to 4.22 points at 32K. These results demonstrate that query-dependent composition of recurrent memory improves long-context modeling and remains effective beyond the training context while using compact per-chunk affine summaries. Project page: https://caesarhhh.github.io/hla/

ru.title: Адаптивное управление памятью: запрос-зависимое внимание для длинных контекстов
ru.desc: Статья представляет Hybrid Linear Attention (HLA) — механизм адаптивного внимания для эффективной обработки длинных контекстов в языковых моделях. HLA решает проблему жесткого сжатия истории в линейном внимании, позволяя моделям динамически выбирать релевантную информацию из предыдущих блоков на основе содержания текущего запроса. Метод использует контент-зависимые параметры маршрутизации для интерполяции исторических переходов состояний, что улучшает способность модели работать с редкой и удалённой информацией. Экспериментальные результаты показывают значительные улучшения производительности на тестах долгоконтекстного моделирования, особенно при экстраполяции за пределы контекста обучения.

en.title: Enhancing Long-Context Modeling with Hybrid Linear Attention
en.desc: This paper presents Hybrid Linear Attention (HLA), a new mechanism designed to enhance long-context autoregressive decoding in machine learning models. HLA allows for better access to historical information by using query-dependent chunk-level attention, which adapts the way past data is accessed based on the current query. The method employs content-dependent routing gates that help manage how historical data is transformed and utilized, improving memory efficiency. Experimental results show that HLA significantly outperforms existing methods, leading to better performance in various tasks involving long-context data.

zh.title: 查询依赖的混合线性注意力提升长上下文建模
zh.desc: 线性注意力通过将历史信息压缩为递归状态，使得长上下文的自回归解码变得高效，但这种压缩可能导致对稀疏和远程信息的选择性访问变得困难。现有的基于块的扩展虽然增加了内存容量，但学习到的块混合系数可能对输入内容保持固定，无法根据每个查询自适应历史访问。我们提出了混合线性注意力（HLA），这是一种针对Gated DeltaNet (GDN) 的查询依赖块级注意力机制。HLA通过紧凑的自注意力池化代表计算内容依赖的路由门，显著提高了长上下文建模的效果。

papers.title: MiniCorp: The Last Mile of the AI Agent Firm
papers.abstract: Abstract  The last mile toward enterprise AGI is a company that runs itself. Training and adapting such agents require longitudinal enterprise data, which remain scarce, costly to acquire, and often restricted by privacy constraints. Historical archives are also frequently incomplete and record only what actually happened. They cannot show the outcomes of alternative decisions. We introduce MiniCorp, an office simulator for studying how agents can collectively run a company while generating enterprise data at scale. Using an e-commerce company as a demonstration, MiniCorp connects two interacting worlds. The external world models customers, dynamic competitors, and market mechanisms. The internal world consists of agents that observe events, discuss their options, and make strategic decisions. These decisions have lasting effects on the market, and the resulting feedback informs the firm's later decisions. As the firm and market interact, MiniCorp continuously records the agents' communications and decisions. These records preserve the information available at the time and the business results that followed. Checkpointing allows the same situation to be replayed under different decisions, providing comparisons unavailable in static archives. We evaluate end-to-end fidelity against patterns reported in empirical studies of real markets. These evaluations provide agents with realistic market feedback and reduce the risk that they learn to exploit flaws in the simulator. Our experiments show agents coordinating across roles and adapting their decisions to market feedback. With explicit long-term strategic guidance, they also sustain advertising exploration despite weak early returns. MiniCorp thus provides an environment for studying AI-run companies and a scalable source of longitudinal and counterfactual enterprise data for agent training and evaluation.

ru.title: Виртуальная компания для обучения агентов самостоятельному управлению бизнесом
ru.desc: Исследователи представили MiniCorp — симулятор офиса, который позволяет изучать, как агенты на основе больших языковых моделей могут коллективно управлять компанией и генерировать корпоративные данные в масштабе. Симулятор объединяет две взаимодействующие среды: внешний мир с клиентами и конкурентами, и внутренний мир с агентами, которые обсуждают стратегию и принимают решения. Система записывает все коммуникации и решения агентов, сохраняя информацию о состоянии и бизнес-результатах, что позволяет проводить контрфактические анализы путём повторного запуска сценариев. Эксперименты показали, что агенты успешно координируют работу, адаптируются к обратной связи рынка и способны следовать долгосрочной стратегии, создавая тем самым ценный источник данных для обучения и оценки AI-агентов.

en.title: MiniCorp: Simulating AI-Driven Companies for Better Decision-Making Insights
en.desc: This paper presents MiniCorp, an innovative office simulator designed to help study how artificial intelligence (AI) agents can manage a company autonomously. It generates large amounts of enterprise data by simulating interactions between agents and external market factors, allowing for the exploration of different decision-making scenarios. MiniCorp enables the replay of situations with varying decisions, providing valuable counterfactual data that traditional historical archives lack. The results demonstrate that agents can effectively coordinate and adapt their strategies based on market feedback, making MiniCorp a significant tool for training and evaluating AI in business contexts.

zh.title: MiniCorp：智能体驱动的企业管理模拟器
zh.desc: 本文介绍了MiniCorp，一个用于研究智能体如何共同管理公司的办公室模拟器。MiniCorp通过模拟外部市场和内部智能体的互动，生成大量企业数据，帮助训练和评估智能体。它允许在不同决策下重放相同情境，从而提供静态档案无法获得的比较。实验表明，智能体能够协调角色并根据市场反馈调整决策，支持AI驱动的公司研究。

papers.title: Towards In-Parameter Memory Augmentation for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract  Recently Large Language Models (LLMs) and LLM-based agents increasingly need to incorporate knowledge acquired after pretraining, e.g., domain facts, user preferences, documents, and interaction experience. In-context learning (ICL) and ICL-based agent harness remain flexible, but they consume context capacity and incur repeated discretized encoding cost that grows with context length. In-parameter memory offers a complementary substrate: reusable memory information is represented in model parameters, adapters, or other parameter-like objects that are composed into the forward pass at inference time. This survey focuses on methods that augment LLMs with such parametric memory at deployment: a memory-bearing parameter object is plugged into the forward pass during inference, whether it is acquired before or during deployment. We organize the landscape with two orthogonal axes: Parameter Placement, which includes Embedding, Attention, FFN layers, or Hybrid when two or more layers are used; and Parameter Acquisition Time, which distinguishes methods whose memory object is acquired during deployment (online) from those acquired before it (offline). We clarify boundaries, conduct comparisons, and discuss open directions in interference, safety, co-design with ICL, and recursive self-improvement.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
